why: PKCE binds an emailed link to the browser that requested it, because the code verifier never leaves that browser's storage. Mail apps open links in the system browser, so the link could never complete and the code was spent regardless. PKCE protects an authorization code travelling through a third-party OAuth redirect; an emailed link to our own origin is not that. The implicit flow returns the session in the URL fragment, which works on any device.
method: The deployed bundle is read to confirm which flow it asks for, then a synthetic unsigned session is presented to the deployed callback in a URL fragment. The tokens are worthless against the provider; what is measured is our own wiring and the state of the address bar afterwards. No email is sent and no account is touched.
note: The synthetic tokens are generated by this script and are unsigned. No real credential appears in this artifact.
forgedSessionNote: The synthetic access token is unsigned, and setSession presented it to GET /auth/v1/user as a bearer. The provider refused it and the callback showed its failure state, so adopting a session from a URL fragment is not a way to fabricate one: the tokens are still validated by the provider before any signed-in state exists.
